title: The Birth of John the Baptist (24 June)
word: The Birth of John the Baptist
hook: with Jesus and Mary, one of only three births in the calendar

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sacred Heart, wounded and burning. Your line was behold this heart. When someone was cold, did you feel the beat first? Day six hundred seventy-four.

Saints are almost always remembered on the day they died. That's the Church's habit: the day of death is the birthday into heaven. But three people get a feast for the day they were born. Jesus, on Christmas. Mary, in September. And one more, today, the twenty-fourth of June, six months before Christmas, near the longest day of the year in the north. In parts of Europe people still light bonfires tonight. The baby whose birth is honored is John, the one who'd grow up to baptize in the Jordan. And his birth starts with a man who can't speak.
screen: `SAINTS: THE DAY THEY DIED.` → `ONLY THREE BIRTHS.` → `A FATHER WHO CAN'T SPEAK.`

segments.voice: Luke tells it. Zachary is an old priest, and his wife Elizabeth has never had children. While he's serving in the Temple, an angel tells him they'll have a son, and Zachary doubts it. So he's struck mute until the day it comes true. Nine months of silence. The baby is born, and on the eighth day the relatives gather for the circumcision and the naming. Everyone assumes he'll be called Zachary, after his father. Elizabeth says no, he'll be called John. They argue: nobody in your family has that name. So they turn to the father and make signs at him. And Zachary, in the Douay-Rheims, "demanding a writing table, he wrote, saying: John is his name." Instantly his tongue is loosed, and he starts praising God. The song he sings, the Benedictus, is prayed by priests and religious every morning in the Liturgy of the Hours. The name John comes from the Hebrew Yohanan, God has been gracious. Choosing it meant breaking with family custom to follow what had been given. And why late June? Luke says Elizabeth was six months along when the angel came to Mary, so the calendar puts John six months before Christmas. Saint Augustine noticed that after John's birth the days start to shorten, and after Christ's they start to lengthen. He heard in it John's own line, from the fourth Gospel: "He must increase: but I must decrease." A whole life pointing past itself, built into the sunlight.
screen: `ZACHARY DOUBTS AND FALLS SILENT.` · `NOBODY IN YOUR FAMILY HAS THAT NAME.` · `YOHANAN: GOD HAS BEEN GRACIOUS.` · `THE DAYS SHORTEN AFTER HIS BIRTH.` · then, large: `HE MUST INCREASE: BUT I MUST DECREASE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold the family you were born into. Sit, and bring them to mind one at a time: parents, brothers and sisters, grandparents, whoever was there at the start. For some people that's easy and warm. For some it's complicated, or painful, or unknown. That's all right; just hold what's true. If you pray, you can pray for each of them by name. If you don't, simply wish each one peace, including anyone you've lost touch with. The bell holds the time.
The Birth of John the Baptist. The twenty-fourth of June, six months before Christmas: one of only three births the Church's calendar keeps. Today's word.
screen: `THE BIRTH OF JOHN THE BAPTIST — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: his name is john. Today, ask someone what their name means, or why they were given it, and listen to the whole story. Day six hundred seventy-four.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Nativity of John the Baptist as a solemnity on 24 June; in parts of Europe and Latin America, Saint John's Eve is kept with bonfires and festivals, and clergy and religious pray his father's song, the Benedictus, every morning.

original.note: Hebrew: Yohanan, God has been gracious — the name Zachary wrote on the tablet.

what it means: one of only three birth feasts, for the man whose whole life pointed past himself.
what a scholar hears: dated from Luke's six months; Augustine linked the shortening days after 24 June to he must increase, but I must decrease.
